title: Indiana University dances and segregation
summary: They play fraternity dances at Indiana University, are the first blacks served in the student union, and learn that black students could not eat there or live on campus.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: But we stayed there and we were able to play down to the University of Indiana, we played the Phi Gam, ma House there, we played for several sororities and our now the band was quite popular with the University of Indiana. At the student union building there, we were the first blacks to be served there. I said that in this vein.

This Gus Wilson who was the brother of Teddy Wilson who played trombone in our band, was a writer. And so I booked Gus to write for the band. So, we had gone by for the band rehearsal and the band rehearsed and the -- and the band leader asked us to stay and join them for dinner, for lunch, which we did and we found out that -- that most coloreds who were going to school there weren't allowed to eat in the building at the time. And, the -- all the colored girls who went to that particular school, they had to stay at a special home, they weren't allowed to stay on the campus. At that time.
That was back in 1933, course there's been many changes since then.
You might as well call it like it is or like it was, you know.
